title: Provisional surge capacity regulator and billing estimator
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity occasionally request temporary burst above their reserved throughput (surge events). Current behavior: we either allow bursts with blunt overage charges or block to meet strict SLOs, producing poor developer experience and surprise invoices. Goal: implement a provisional surge regulator that applies short-lived, meterable boosts with controlled decay and a real-time invoice estimator so tenants know expected overage exposure before/after surge events.

Scope and success criteria:
- Implement regulator that grants provisional token/slot-level boosts for a configurable window (default 10 minutes) with decay scheduling.
- Autoscaling coordination: regulator must request increased allocation from fleet autoscaler when sustained usage exceeds threshold, but not for transient spikes below X% duration.
- Overage estimator: provide tenant-facing and operator-facing delta estimates (per-minute and 24h projection) tied to current boosts and throttles.
- Billing behavior: define prorated overage attribution rules, credit/clawback handling for rapid reversals, and invoice line items that explain provisional boosts.
- Preserve SLOs for high-priority tenants by fencing surge pools and enabling tenant priority weights.

Design decisions considered (trade-offs):
1) Conservative granting vs permissive granting: conservative approach minimizes SLO risk but increases customer friction; permissive increases short-term availability but risks sustained overprovisioned spend and noisy neighbor problems. We will apply a hybrid rule: short permissive window with rapid decay + autoscaler escalation if usage persists beyond window.
2) Charge immediately vs delayed reconciliation: charging immediately is simpler but causes surprise invoices; delayed reconciliation reduces surprise but requires more complex accounting and operator tooling. We will surface an immediate provisional estimate and reconcile at end-of-window with clear line items.
3) Central surge pool vs per-tenant micro pools: central pool is easier to manage but single point of contention; per-tenant micro pools are fairer but consume capacity planning. We'll start with a central pool with soft tenant quotas and expand to per-tenant pools for high-tier customers.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (spike-safe regulator prototype): implement regulator admission logic and short boost grant API; hook into existing quota manager. Provide operator metrics: grants/sec, avg boost duration, rejection rate. (Weeks 1-2)
- Phase 2 (autoscaler integration & decay policy): wire regulator to fleet autoscaler, implement decay scheduler and per-grant TTL enforcement, add canary tenants to test escalation. (Weeks 3-4)
- Phase 3 (billing estimator & invoicing rules): build estimator service that consumes grant stream and token usage, produce realtime estimate UI and daily reconciliation job; finalize invoice format. (Week 5)
- Phase 4 (hardening & rollout): add tenant fencing, priority weights, and runbook for operator dispute resolution. Add configurable guardrails in Console. (Week 6)

Metrics to monitor:
- Boost grants per tenant and per pool
- Mean boost duration and decay curve adherence
- Fraction of boosts that led to autoscaler escalation
- Estimated vs actual overage (delta) after reconciliation
- SLO violation rate for fenced tenants

Open questions:
- What should the default boost window be for general customers? Proposal: 10 minutes with exponential decay.
- Granularity of billing estimator: per-request token-level vs hourly aggregate. Proposal: per-minute aggregates exposed to users, hourly/daily aggregates for invoices.
- Operator controls for emergency revocation: will revocation be immediate or phased? Proposal: immediate for security events, phased for cost events.

Attachments and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/surge-regulator-proposal (draft)
- Initial load test results (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/abc123-loadtests (prototype spike tests)
- Related Linear: ENG-33123 (elastic-headroom-manager), ENG-41234 (transient-headroom-allocator)
- PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1267

Operator playbook (short):
- If tenant disputes invoice: run reconciliation job for their grant window, show provisional estimate vs reconciled charge, if discrepancy > 20% open billing review.
- If surge pool saturation > 80%: automatically throttle permissive grants, escalate to SRE to scale fleet or enable temporary tenant-level caps.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Complete regulator prototype and unit tests (ENG)
- Wire basic grant metrics into Console dev dashboard (Console/Observability)
- Draft invoice line item schema with Finance for legal review
